description:
Where a wallet's USDC on Base came from: every address that sent it USDC, with amounts, transfer counts and block ranges. A sender that is a contract (an escrow refund, a router, a bridge) is marked as a return path, not a funder.
Call it on a line: a call without one has only a moment, enough for a small range of recent blocks, and is cut, uncharged, when it needs longer. from_block is a block number and defaults to the whole history; Base adds about 43,200 blocks a day. The first answer says how many windows the scan will take and about how many milliseconds, at the pace of recent scans, and each one after says how many are done.
$0.000001 per millisecond on a line.
Paid, on a line. With no wallet code, a pass (https://mcp.zeamprism.com/pass) or the Bridge buys the time and opens the line for you: https://mcp.zeamprism.com/how-to-pay
Example: {"address":"0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD","from_block":51000000}

from_block.description: optional int — the block to start from; default the whole history. If the line runs out mid-scan you get what was scanned so far, marked partial; continue with to_block set to one below scanned.from.

line.description: optional — a line credential: the call burns the line's time and carries no payment.

to_block.description: optional int — stop; default the head.

token.description: optional string — the asset to follow, 0x form; default USDC.

window.description: optional int — blocks per snapshot, default 10000; smaller gives a short line its first snapshot sooner.
